decisions.label: SUPPORTED

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r3 report 3.9 versus 4.5 seconds under the same timing setup; the approximately 13% reduction reasonably supports “slightly lower.”

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r3 show FID falling from 15.6 to 7.8—exactly a halving—so “much lower” is calibrated to the reported magnitude.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 report 8 versus 50 NFE, a reduction of 84%; this directly supports a marked efficiency advantage in evaluations.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 report 0.94 versus 5.40 TFLOPs per image, an approximately 83% reduction that supports “markedly more efficient.”

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 report 3.9 versus 21.7 seconds per batch under matched conditions, an approximately 82% reduction supporting “markedly more efficient.”

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: The package contains only exp1 on Halvern-Faces at 256×256 and one specified setup, but no source text explicitly states the numeric count “single”; therefore no direct numeric mapping is available.

decisions.label: OVERSTATED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 establish the efficiency–FID tradeoff only on Halvern-Faces. Omitting that dataset limitation makes the general “256×256 face generation” scope broader than the evidence.

decisions.label: SUPPORTED
decisions.rationale: T1.r1 and T1.r2 show large reductions in all efficiency measures alongside a comparatively small FID increase from 7.1 to 7.8; “modest” is a calibrated magnitude description, not a significance claim.
